source.candidate: ordered root-statistics updates and simulation-time node counting

canonical_throughput.method: Two adjacent unprofiled runs per implementation on the same host; arithmetic means summarize the recorded runs. The baseline is the immediately preceding retained expansion implementation recorded in mini-mcts-expansion-initialization.json.

equivalence.golden_test: The seeded 5x5 sparse-policy search retains the complete serialized move and metadata SHA-256, and an ordered-view regression compares every public root statistic with root_moves and inspection.candidates.

metadata_microbenchmark.method: Seven samples of 20000 calls on one synthetic 80-move root with four expanded children, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, on CPU; median time includes ordered MCTSMoveStatistics, root_moves, and inspection.candidates construction. The reference reproduces the replaced root-child dictionary and per-legal-move hash lookup.

rejected_approaches.implementation: build statistics, root_moves, and inspection candidates together in one explicit Python loop
rejected_approaches.reason_rejected: Two canonical trials took 70.566 s and 70.776 s (70.671 s mean), slower than the 70.617 s baseline mean. Replacing the list comprehensions with repeated append calls erased the intended saving.

rejected_approaches.implementation: map every legal root move through a root-child dictionary in a single statistics comprehension
rejected_approaches.reason_rejected: It removed one statistics pass but retained a PegPlacement hash lookup for every legal move. The local 80-move benchmark was 0.93x the reference, while updating only expanded entries by their identity-preserving tuple index measured 1.21x.

rejected_approaches.implementation: remove or lazily expose last_statistics, root_moves, or inspection.candidates
rejected_approaches.reason_rejected: All three are public inspection surfaces. Deferring or changing their concrete construction could alter mutation timing, serialization behavior, or caller-observed types instead of preserving the existing contract.
